rules.rule_name: Identify Input Queue for Closure
rules.rule_description: Before closing the input queue, the program identifies the correct input queue by associating the input queue name and its active handle to ensure the correct queue is targeted for closure.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Identify Input Queue for Closure

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has completed processing all messages or a termination condition has been triggered, and the input queue was previously opened successfully (REPLY-QUEUE-OPEN flag is TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The program prepares to close the input queue
acceptance_criteria.Then: The input queue name (INPUT-QUEUE-NAME) and its corresponding active queue handle (INPUT-QUEUE-HANDLE) are set as the target identifiers for the closure operation

rules.rule_name: Attempt to Close Input Queue
rules.rule_description: The program attempts to formally close the input queue using the queue manager to release the queue resource after all message processing is complete or upon termination.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Attempt to Close Input Queue

acceptance_criteria.Given: The input queue name and handle have been identified and the queue is currently open
acceptance_criteria.When: The program invokes the queue close operation (MQCLOSE) using the queue manager connection, the input queue handle, and standard close options (MQCO-NONE)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The queue manager processes the closure request and returns a condition code and reason code indicating success or failure

rules.rule_name: Input Queue Closed Successfully
rules.rule_description: When the input queue is closed without errors, the program records the successful closure outcome and proceeds to close the output reply queue.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Input Queue Closed Successfully

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has attempted to close the input queue
acceptance_criteria.When: The queue manager returns a successful condition code (MQCC-OK) for the close operation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The condition code and reason code from the queue manager are recorded, and the program proceeds to the next step of closing the output reply queue

rules.rule_name: Log Input Queue Closure Error Details
rules.rule_description: When the input queue cannot be closed successfully, the program captures and records the error details including the error condition, reason, and the name of the queue that failed to close, to support error diagnosis.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Log Queue Closure Error - Capture Error Details & Queue Name

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has attempted to close the input queue
acceptance_criteria.When: The queue manager returns a condition code other than success (not MQCC-OK) for the close operation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The error condition code is recorded in the application condition code field, the error reason code is recorded in the application reason code field, the input queue name (INPUT-QUEUE-NAME) is recorded in the application queue name field, and the error message 'MQCLOSE ERR' is recorded in the application return message field

rules.rule_name: Trigger Program Termination on Input Queue Closure Failure
rules.rule_description: When the input queue fails to close, the program cannot continue normal operations and must initiate a full program termination sequence to ensure all remaining open queues are properly closed and resources are released.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Trigger Program Termination

acceptance_criteria.Given: The input queue closure has failed and the error details have been logged
acceptance_criteria.When: The closure failure condition is confirmed (condition code is not MQCC-OK)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program immediately invokes the termination routine (8000-TERMINATION), which closes any remaining open queues (output reply queue and error queue if open) and ends the program execution

rules.rule_name: Conditional Execution of Input Queue Closure
rules.rule_description: The input queue closure is only attempted if the input queue was successfully opened during program initialization, preventing errors from attempting to close a queue that was never opened.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Input Queue Closure Triggered

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program termination sequence has been initiated either due to normal end-of-messages or an error condition
acceptance_criteria.When: The termination routine (8000-TERMINATION) evaluates whether the input queue is open
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the REPLY-QUEUE-OPEN flag is TRUE (indicating the input queue was successfully opened), the input queue closure routine is performed; if the flag is FALSE, the input queue closure step is skipped entirely

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has reached the termination phase and the reply output queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT) was previously opened for sending account inquiry responses
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initiates the closure of the reply output queue
acceptance_criteria.Then: The reply output queue named CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT and its associated queue handle (OUTPUT-QUEUE-HANDLE) are identified and set as the target for the closure operation

acceptance_criteria.When: The queue closure operation is executed for the reply output queue
acceptance_criteria.Then: The closure operation is attempted using the queue connection handle (MQ-HCONN), the output queue handle (OUTPUT-QUEUE-HANDLE), and standard closure options (MQCO-NONE), and the resulting condition code and reason code are captured for evaluation

rules.rule_name: Successful Reply Output Queue Closure
rules.rule_description: When the reply output queue is closed successfully, the program acknowledges the successful release of queue resources and records the outcome.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Reply Output Queue
Closed Successfully
Resources Released

acceptance_criteria.Given: The closure operation has been executed for the reply output queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT
acceptance_criteria.When: The queue closure operation completes with a successful condition code (MQCC-OK)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The reply output queue resources are released, and the resulting condition code and reason code from the closure operation are recorded as the application condition code (MQ-APPL-CONDITION-CODE) and application reason code (MQ-APPL-REASON-CODE) respectively, and processing proceeds to program termination

rules.rule_name: Record Reply Output Queue Closure Failure Details
rules.rule_description: When the reply output queue closure fails, the program must capture and record all relevant failure details including the queue name, error description, condition code, and reason code for diagnostic and audit purposes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Record Closure Failure Details
Queue Name, Error Description,
Condition Code, Reason Code

acceptance_criteria.Given: The closure operation has been executed for the reply output queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT
acceptance_criteria.When: The queue closure operation completes with any condition code other than successful (not MQCC-OK)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The failure details are recorded as follows: the condition code from the closure attempt is stored as the application condition code (MQ-APPL-CONDITION-CODE), the reason code from the closure attempt is stored as the application reason code (MQ-APPL-REASON-CODE), the input queue name is recorded as the application queue name (MQ-APPL-QUEUE-NAME), and the error description 'MQCLOSE ERR' is recorded as the application return message (MQ-APPL-RETURN-MESSAGE)

rules.rule_name: Initiate Program Termination on Reply Queue Closure Failure
rules.rule_description: When the reply output queue cannot be closed successfully, the program must immediately proceed to the termination routine to ensure all remaining resources are properly handled.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Proceed to
Program Termination

acceptance_criteria.Given: The reply output queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT closure has failed and the failure details (condition code, reason code, queue name, and error description 'MQCLOSE ERR') have been recorded
acceptance_criteria.When: The closure failure is confirmed with a non-successful condition code
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program immediately invokes the termination routine (8000-TERMINATION) to close any remaining open queues (input queue, error queue) and end the program, without sending an error notification to the error queue

rules.rule_name: Initiate Error Queue Closure During Program Termination
rules.rule_description: During program termination, the error queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) must be closed only if it was previously opened, to ensure proper release of queue resources.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 19: Error Queue Closure - Begin Closing CARD.DEMO.ERROR

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has reached the termination phase and the error queue CARD.DEMO.ERROR has been successfully opened during the current program execution (ERR-QUEUE-OPEN flag is TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initiates the closure of the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue as part of the termination sequence
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program proceeds to attempt closing the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue; if the error queue was never opened, this closure step is skipped entirely

rules.rule_name: Successful Error Queue Closure Confirmation
rules.rule_description: When the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue is successfully closed during program termination, the closure outcome is recorded and the program continues to complete its termination sequence.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Queue Closed Successfully? - Yes → Error Queue Closed Successfully, Resources Released

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has attempted to close the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue during the termination phase
acceptance_criteria.When: The queue closure operation completes successfully without any errors
acceptance_criteria.Then: The successful closure status and associated reason details are recorded internally, the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue resources are released, and the program continues to the final termination step (CICS RETURN)

rules.rule_name: Error Queue Closure Failure - Send Error Notification
rules.rule_description: When the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue cannot be closed during program termination, the failure details including the queue name and a closure error message must be formatted and sent as an error notification before forcing program termination.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 16: Send Error Notification - Format and send closure failure details to error queue

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has attempted to close the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue during the termination phase, and the closure operation has failed
acceptance_criteria.When: The queue closure returns a non-successful outcome
acceptance_criteria.Then: The failure condition details, reason details, the queue name CARD.DEMO.ERROR, and the error message 'MQCLOSE ERR' are captured; an error notification containing these details is formatted and sent to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR error queue; and the program is forced into immediate termination

rules.rule_name: Force Program Termination After Error Queue Closure Failure
rules.rule_description: When the error queue CARD.DEMO.ERROR cannot be closed successfully, the program must not continue normal processing and must force an immediate termination after attempting to log the error.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: No - Closure Failed → Force Program Termination

acceptance_criteria.Given: The closure of the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue has failed during the termination phase, and the error notification has been sent
acceptance_criteria.When: The error notification process completes (regardless of whether the notification itself succeeded)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program forces immediate termination by closing any remaining open queues (input queue if open, output/reply queue if open) and issuing a CICS RETURN to end the program execution; no further message processing occurs

rules.rule_name: Conditional Release of Input Queue During Shutdown
rules.rule_description: During program termination, the system must check whether the Input Queue is currently open before attempting to release it, to ensure only active queue connections are closed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Input Queue Currently Open?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program termination sequence has been triggered
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the Input Queue (identified by INPUT-QUEUE-NAME and INPUT-QUEUE-HANDLE) is currently in an open state
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Input Queue is open, the system proceeds to close it and release its resources; if it is already closed, the system skips the close step and moves on to check the Reply Queue

rules.rule_name: Release of Input Queue Resources at Shutdown
rules.rule_description: When the Input Queue is confirmed open during shutdown, the system must formally close the Input Queue to release all associated message queue resources.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Close Input Queue
Release input message queue resources

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program termination sequence is in progress and the Input Queue (INPUT-QUEUE-NAME) is currently open with a valid queue handle (INPUT-QUEUE-HANDLE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the close operation against the Input Queue using the established queue connection
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Input Queue is successfully closed and its resources are released; if the close operation fails, the termination sequence is re-invoked to handle the failure

rules.rule_name: Conditional Release of Reply Queue During Shutdown
rules.rule_description: During program termination, the system must check whether the Reply (Output) Queue is currently open before attempting to release it, ensuring only active connections are closed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Reply Queue Currently Open?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program termination sequence is in progress and the Input Queue check has been completed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the Reply Queue (identified by REPLY-QUEUE-NAME and OUTPUT-QUEUE-HANDLE) is currently in an open state
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Reply Queue is open, the system proceeds to close it and release its resources; if it is already closed, the system skips the close step and moves on to check the Error Queue

rules.rule_name: Release of Reply Queue Resources at Shutdown
rules.rule_description: When the Reply Queue is confirmed open during shutdown, the system must formally close the Reply Output Queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT) to release all associated message queue resources.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Close Reply Output Queue
Release reply message queue resources

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program termination sequence is in progress and the Reply Queue (REPLY-QUEUE-NAME: CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT) is currently open with a valid queue handle (OUTPUT-QUEUE-HANDLE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the close operation against the Reply Output Queue using the established queue connection
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Reply Queue is successfully closed and its resources are released; if the close operation fails, the termination sequence is re-invoked to handle the failure

rules.rule_name: Conditional Release of Error Queue During Shutdown
rules.rule_description: During program termination, the system must check whether the Error Queue is currently open before attempting to release it, ensuring only active connections are closed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Error Queue Currently Open?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program termination sequence is in progress and both the Input Queue and Reply Queue checks have been completed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the Error Queue (identified by ERROR-QUEUE-NAME: CARD.DEMO.ERROR and ERROR-QUEUE-HANDLE) is currently in an open state
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Error Queue is open, the system proceeds to close it and release its resources; if it is already closed, the system skips the close step and proceeds to return control to CICS

rules.rule_name: Release of Error Queue Resources at Shutdown
rules.rule_description: When the Error Queue is confirmed open during shutdown, the system must formally close the Error Queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) to release all associated message queue resources.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Close Error Queue
Release error message queue resources

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program termination sequence is in progress and the Error Queue (ERROR-QUEUE-NAME: CARD.DEMO.ERROR) is currently open with a valid queue handle (ERROR-QUEUE-HANDLE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the close operation against the Error Queue using the established queue connection
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Error Queue is successfully closed and its resources are released; if the close operation fails, an error notification is sent to the Error Queue and the termination sequence is re-invoked

rules.rule_name: Ordered Queue Closure Sequence During Shutdown
rules.rule_description: The program termination must follow a strict sequential order when closing queues: Input Queue first, then Reply Queue, then Error Queue, ensuring an orderly and complete release of all messaging resources.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Program Termination Triggered

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program termination sequence has been triggered either by normal end-of-messages or by a system error condition
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs the shutdown sequence
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must close queues in the following mandatory order: (1) Input Queue, (2) Reply Output Queue, (3) Error Queue — and only close each queue if it is currently open, skipping any queue that was never opened or already closed

rules.rule_name: Return Control to CICS After Queue Cleanup
rules.rule_description: After all open queues have been closed, the program must formally return control to the CICS transaction manager, signaling the end of the program's execution.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Return Control to CICS
Program Ends

acceptance_criteria.Given: All open queues (Input, Reply, and Error) have been evaluated and closed as applicable during the termination sequence
acceptance_criteria.When: The system has completed all queue closure operations
acceptance_criteria.Then: Control is returned to CICS and the program terminates, making no further processing of account inquiry messages

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account inquiry service program is triggered to start
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program begins execution
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All queue name fields (Input Queue Name, Queue Manager Name), message fields (Queue Message), and error display fields are cleared to spaces and initialized to their default empty values before any processing begins

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Initialization - Clear Working Storage
all_rules.Rule_Description: At program startup, all working storage fields including queue names and message fields are cleared to ensure no residual data affects processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has completed initialization of working storage fields
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the error queue named 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR' for writing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the error queue opens successfully, the error queue handle is saved and the error queue status is marked as open, allowing subsequent error messages to be written to 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR'; if the error queue fails to open, the error details are displayed and the program terminates immediately

all_rules.Rule_Name: Error Queue Setup - Open CARD.DEMO.ERROR for Writing
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before any business processing begins, the dedicated error queue must be opened for output so that any subsequent errors can be captured and routed appropriately.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The error queue has been successfully opened and the program is ready to identify its input source
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program retrieves the CICS trigger message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The trigger message data (MQTM) is retrieved and made available for extracting the input queue name; if retrieval fails, the CICS response codes are captured and an error message is composed containing 'CICS RETREIVE' as the error paragraph identifier along with the response codes, the error is sent to the error queue, and the program terminates

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Trigger Retrieval - Retrieve CICS Trigger Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program retrieves the CICS trigger message that initiated this transaction. The trigger message contains the name of the input queue to process.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program attempted to retrieve the CICS trigger message
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The CICS RETRIEVE command does not return a NORMAL response
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error paragraph is identified as 'CICS RETREIVE', the CICS response codes (RESP1 and RESP2) are formatted into an error message prefixed with 'RESP: ', the error message is written to the 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR' queue, and the program proceeds to termination closing all open queues

all_rules.Rule_Name: CICS Retrieve Failure - Terminate with Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the CICS trigger message cannot be retrieved, an error notification is sent to the error queue and the program terminates without processing any account inquiries.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The CICS trigger message has been successfully retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program processes the trigger message content
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The input queue name is set to the queue name extracted from the trigger message field MQTM-QNAME, and the reply queue name is set to the hardcoded value 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Input Queue Identification - Extract Queue Name and Set Reply Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful trigger message retrieval, the input queue name is dynamically extracted from the trigger message, and the reply queue is set to the fixed destination 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT'.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The input queue name has been identified from the trigger message
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program opens the input queue for reading
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the input queue opens successfully, the input queue handle is saved and the reply queue status is marked as open (REPLY-QUEUE-OPEN = TRUE), enabling message retrieval; if the input queue fails to open, the queue name is recorded as 'INPUT-QUEUE-NAME', the error message 'INP MQOPEN ERR' is sent to the error queue, and the program terminates

all_rules.Rule_Name: Input Queue Open - Open Account Inquiry Request Queue for Shared Reading
all_rules.Rule_Description: The input queue identified from the trigger message is opened in shared read mode so that account inquiry request messages can be retrieved for processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The input queue has been successfully opened and the reply queue name is set to 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program opens the reply output queue for writing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the reply queue opens successfully, the output queue handle is saved and the response queue status is marked as open (RESP-QUEUE-OPEN = TRUE), enabling response delivery; if the reply queue fails to open, the queue name is recorded as 'REPLY-QUEUE-NAME', the error message 'OUT MQOPEN ERR' is sent to the error queue, and the program terminates

all_rules.Rule_Name: Output Reply Queue Open - Open CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT for Writing Responses
all_rules.Rule_Description: The fixed reply queue 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT' is opened for writing so that account inquiry responses can be delivered back to the requesting system.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Both the input queue and reply queue have been successfully opened
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to retrieve the first message from the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program waits up to 5,000 milliseconds (5 seconds) for a message; the message ID and correlation ID are cleared before retrieval; if a message is retrieved, it is placed into the message buffer (1,000 byte buffer) and processing continues; if no message is available within 5 seconds, the NO-MORE-MSGS condition is set and the program proceeds to termination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initial Message Retrieval - Retrieve First Message with 5-Second Wait
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program attempts to retrieve the first account inquiry request message from the input queue, waiting up to 5 seconds for a message to become available.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to retrieve a message from the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The result of the message retrieval is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If a message was successfully retrieved (NO-MORE-MSGS is false), the program proceeds to parse and process the message; if no message was available (NO-MORE-MSGS is true), the program proceeds to close all queues and terminate

all_rules.Rule_Name: Message Availability Check - Determine if More Messages Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: After each message retrieval attempt, the program checks whether a message was successfully retrieved to determine if processing should continue or if the program should terminate.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A message has been processed and a reply has been sent to the reply queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program prepares to retrieve the next message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A CICS SYNCPOINT is executed to commit the current transaction (making the reply permanent), and then the next message is retrieved from the input queue with a 5,000 millisecond wait interval; the loop continues until no more messages are available

all_rules.Rule_Name: Message Processing Loop - Commit and Retrieve Next Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: After each message is processed and a reply is sent, the transaction is committed via a CICS syncpoint before retrieving the next message, ensuring each reply is permanently committed before moving on.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A message has been successfully retrieved from the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program parses the incoming message content
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The function code (WS-FUNC) and account key (WS-KEY) are extracted from the message; these two fields are used to validate and route the request for further processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Request Message Parsing - Extract Function Code and Account Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each retrieved message is parsed to extract the function code (WS-FUNC) and the account key (WS-KEY) which are the two critical fields that determine how the request will be processed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A message has been parsed and the function code (WS-FUNC) and account key (WS-KEY) have been extracted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program evaluates the request validity
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the function code equals 'INQA' AND the account key is greater than zero, the request is considered valid and proceeds to account lookup; if either condition is not met (function code is not 'INQA' OR account key is zero or blank), the request is treated as invalid and an invalid request response is built

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Inquiry Request Validation - Function Code and Account Key Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Every incoming request is validated to ensure it contains the correct function code 'INQA' and a non-zero account key before any account lookup is performed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The request has been validated with function code 'INQA' and account key greater than zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program prepares for the account record lookup
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The account key value (WS-KEY) is moved into the account record ID field (WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID) which will be used as the search key to read the account record from the ACCTDAT file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Inquiry Validation - Set Account ID for Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a valid INQA request is confirmed, the account key from the request message is assigned as the account ID to be used for the account file lookup.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid account inquiry request has been received with function code 'INQA' and a non-zero account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reads the account record from the ACCTDAT file using the account ID (WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X) as the key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the account record is found, all account fields are made available for response building; if the account is not found, an account-not-found response is prepared; if a file access error occurs, the error details are sent to the error queue and the program terminates

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Record Lookup - Read Account from ACCTDAT by Account ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: The account record is retrieved from the ACCTDAT (Account File - VSAM) using the account ID as the unique key to fetch all account details.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account record has been successfully retrieved from the ACCTDAT file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program builds the account inquiry response
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The following account fields are populated into the response (WS-ACCT-RESPONSE): Account ID (ACCT-ID), Account Active Status (ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS), Current Balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL), Credit Limit (ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT), Cash Credit Limit (ACCT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT), Account Open Date (ACCT-OPEN-DATE), Account Expiration Date (ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE), Account Reissue Date (ACCT-REISSUE-DATE), Current Cycle Credits (ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT), Current Cycle Debits (ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT), and Account Group ID (ACCT-GROUP-ID); the assembled response is then moved to the reply message field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Data Response Building - Populate Full Account Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account record is successfully found, all relevant account fields are extracted and assembled into the response message to be returned to the requesting system.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid INQA request was received with a non-zero account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The account record is not found in the ACCTDAT file for the provided account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: An error response message is built containing the text 'INVALID REQUEST PARAMETERS ACCT ID : ' followed by the account key value (WS-KEY), this message is placed into the reply message field, and the response is sent to the reply queue 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT'; the program continues processing subsequent messages without terminating

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Not Found Response - Build Invalid Request Error for Missing Account
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the requested account ID does not exist in the account file, an error response message is constructed indicating the account was not found, and processing continues for subsequent messages.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A message has been retrieved from the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The function code (WS-FUNC) is not equal to 'INQA' OR the account key (WS-KEY) is zero or blank
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: An error response message is built containing the text 'INVALID REQUEST PARAMETERS ACCT ID : ' followed by the account key value (WS-KEY) and 'FUNCTION : ' followed by the function code value (WS-FUNC), this message is placed into the reply message field, and the response is sent to the reply queue 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT'; the program continues processing subsequent messages without terminating

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invalid Request Response - Build Error for Bad Function Code or Zero Account Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a request fails validation because the function code is not 'INQA' or the account key is zero, an error response is built identifying both the invalid account ID and the invalid function code.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A response message has been built (either account data, account not found error, or invalid request error)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program sends the response to the reply queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The reply message is placed onto the 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT' queue with a buffer length of 1,000 bytes, the message format is set to string format, the original message ID (SAVE-MSGID) is preserved in the message descriptor, the original correlation ID (SAVE-CORELID) is preserved to allow the requester to correlate the reply, and the message is sent within the current syncpoint scope; if the put operation fails, the error details including queue name 'REPLY-QUEUE-NAME' and message 'MQPUT ERR' are sent to the error queue and the program terminates

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reply Message Delivery - Send Response to CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT
all_rules.Rule_Description: All responses (successful account data, account not found, or invalid request) are delivered to the reply queue with proper message correlation so the requesting system can match the reply to its original request.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All messages have been processed from the input queue and the NO-MORE-MSGS condition is set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initiates termination and the input queue is marked as open (REPLY-QUEUE-OPEN is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The input queue is closed using the saved input queue handle; if closure fails, the error details including queue name and message 'MQCLOSE ERR' are recorded and the program proceeds to termination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Input Queue Closure - Close Account Inquiry Request Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all messages have been processed, the input queue is closed to release the queue resource.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The input queue has been closed and the reply output queue is marked as open (RESP-QUEUE-OPEN is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program closes the reply output queue 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The reply queue is closed using the saved output queue handle; if closure fails, the error details including queue name and message 'MQCLOSE ERR' are recorded and the program proceeds to termination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Output Reply Queue Closure - Close CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all replies have been sent and the input queue is closed, the reply output queue is closed to release the queue resource.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Both the input queue and reply queue have been closed and the error queue is marked as open (ERR-QUEUE-OPEN is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program closes the error queue 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error queue is closed using the saved error queue handle; if closure fails, the error details including queue name and message 'MQCLOSE ERR' are sent to the error queue itself and the program proceeds to termination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Error Queue Closure - Close CARD.DEMO.ERROR Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: As the final queue closure step, the error queue is closed after all other queues have been closed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has completed all message processing or encountered a terminal error condition
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initiates the termination sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Each queue is conditionally closed only if it was previously opened: the input queue is closed if REPLY-QUEUE-OPEN is TRUE, the reply output queue is closed if RESP-QUEUE-OPEN is TRUE, and the error queue is closed if ERR-QUEUE-OPEN is TRUE; after all open queues are closed, control is returned to CICS via EXEC CICS RETURN

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Termination - Orderly Shutdown and Return to CICS
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program performs an orderly shutdown by closing only the queues that were successfully opened, then returns control to CICS.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Inquiry Service program has been triggered and is starting a new processing session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program begins its initialization sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Input Queue Name field must be set to blank spaces, removing any previously held or residual queue name value before the queue name is dynamically assigned from the trigger message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Input Queue Name at Program Start
all_rules.Rule_Description: At program startup, the Input Queue Name field must be cleared to blank spaces to ensure no residual or stale queue name data influences the current processing session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Inquiry Service program has been triggered and is starting a new processing session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program begins its initialization sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Queue Manager Name field must be set to blank spaces, ensuring the queue manager reference is clean and ready to be populated from the trigger message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Queue Manager Name at Program Start
all_rules.Rule_Description: At program startup, the Queue Manager Name field must be cleared to blank spaces to ensure no stale queue manager reference is carried into the current processing session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Inquiry Service program has been triggered and is starting a new processing session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program begins its initialization sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Queue Message field must be set to blank spaces, ensuring the message buffer is empty and ready to receive new incoming account inquiry messages

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Queue Message Fields at Program Start
all_rules.Rule_Description: At program startup, the Queue Message field must be cleared to blank spaces to ensure no residual message content from a prior execution affects the current session's message processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Inquiry Service program has been triggered and is starting a new processing session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program begins its initialization sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All error display and error tracking fields (MQ-ERR-DISPLAY) must be initialized to their default values, ensuring that any error information captured during the session reflects only errors from the current run and not from any prior execution

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Error Display Fields at Program Start
all_rules.Rule_Description: At program startup, all error tracking and error display fields must be reset to their initial default values to ensure accurate error reporting throughout the current processing session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Inquiry Service program has been triggered to start
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program executes its startup initialization sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All four initialization steps must complete in the following strict order before any queue is opened: (1) Input Queue Name is set to blank spaces, (2) Queue Manager Name is set to blank spaces, (3) Queue Message field is set to blank spaces, (4) Error Display fields are initialized to default values — only after all four steps are complete does the program proceed to open the Error Queue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Complete Initialization Before Queue Setup
all_rules.Rule_Description: All working storage fields — including Input Queue Name, Queue Manager Name, Queue Message, and Error Display fields — must be fully cleared and initialized before the program proceeds to open any queues. This ensures a clean and consistent state for the entire processing session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is initializing its error handling infrastructure at startup
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The error queue setup process begins
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error queue name must be set to the fixed value 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR', which is the sole designated queue for capturing all error messages generated during account inquiry processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Error Queue Name Assignment
all_rules.Rule_Description: The error queue name is always statically assigned to 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR' as the designated destination for all system error messages. This is a fixed business configuration that does not vary by request or context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is starting up and the error queue name has been set to 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the error queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error queue 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR' must be opened with output (write) access and with context-passing enabled, so that error messages can be written to it throughout the program's lifecycle; this step must complete before any other queue is opened or any message processing begins

all_rules.Rule_Name: Error Queue Must Be Opened for Writing Before Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before any account inquiry processing begins, the program must establish write access to the error queue 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR'. This ensures that any errors encountered during processing can be captured and routed appropriately.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to open the error queue 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR' for writing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The queue is opened successfully without any errors
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error queue must be flagged as open and available (ERR-QUEUE-OPEN = TRUE) and the queue handle must be saved for use by all subsequent error-writing operations during the program's execution

all_rules.Rule_Name: Error Queue Successfully Opened — Mark as Ready
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the error queue 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR' is successfully opened for writing, the program records its availability status so that subsequent error-handling routines know they can safely route error messages to it.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to open the error queue 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR' for writing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The queue fails to open for any reason
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must display the full error details (including queue name 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR', error condition code, and error reason code) to the system log, and then immediately terminate all processing — no input queue, output queue, or account inquiry messages may be processed under any circumstances when the error queue is unavailable

all_rules.Rule_Name: Error Queue Unavailable — Terminate Program
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the error queue 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR' cannot be opened, the program cannot safely handle any errors that may arise during processing. Therefore, the program must log the failure details and immediately terminate without processing any account inquiry messages.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The error queue 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR' could not be opened and error details have been displayed to the system log
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The termination process is triggered due to error queue unavailability
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must close any queues that were successfully opened prior to this failure (input queue if open, output queue if open, error queue if open), and then return control to the CICS system — no account inquiry messages are retrieved or processed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Termination When Error Queue Is Unavailable
all_rules.Rule_Description: The inability to open the error queue is treated as a fatal condition. The program must perform an orderly shutdown, closing any queues that were already opened, before returning control to the calling system.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has been triggered by a CICS trigger mechanism and the error queue has been successfully opened
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to retrieve the triggering transaction message from CICS
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The CICS trigger message (MQTM) is retrieved and the retrieval response codes (RESP and RESP2) are captured for evaluation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Triggering Transaction Information from CICS
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program must retrieve the triggering transaction message from CICS at startup to obtain the input queue name that initiated this program execution.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The CICS trigger message has been successfully retrieved with a NORMAL response
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The retrieval response is confirmed as successful (DFHRESP NORMAL)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The queue name field (MQTM-QNAME) from the trigger message is extracted and stored as the INPUT-QUEUE-NAME to be used for reading incoming account inquiry requests

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract Input Queue Name from Successful Trigger Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the CICS trigger message is successfully retrieved, the input queue name must be extracted from the trigger message to identify the source queue for account inquiry requests.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The CICS trigger message has been successfully retrieved and the input queue name has been extracted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program sets up the reply destination for account inquiry responses
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The reply queue name is always set to the fixed value 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT', regardless of the originating request source or input queue name

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Fixed Reply Queue Destination for Account Inquiry Responses
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful trigger retrieval, the reply queue where all account inquiry responses will be sent must be set to the fixed, hardcoded destination queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The CICS trigger message retrieval has been attempted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The retrieval response is not NORMAL (retrieval failed)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error context is captured as follows: the error paragraph name is set to 'CICS RETREIVE', the CICS condition code (WS-CICS-RESP1-CD) is moved to its display field (WS-CICS-RESP1-CD-D), the CICS reason code (WS-CICS-RESP2-CD) is retained, and an error message is constructed by concatenating 'RESP: ', the condition code display value, the reason code display value, and 'END' into the MQ-APPL-RETURN-MESSAGE field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Error Details on Failed Trigger Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the CICS trigger message retrieval fails, the error context must be captured including the operation name, condition code, and reason code to support error notification and diagnostics.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The CICS trigger message retrieval has failed and the error details including condition code, reason code, and error message have been captured
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The error notification process is invoked (9000-ERROR)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error details stored in MQ-ERR-DISPLAY are placed into the error message buffer and sent to the error queue CARD.DEMO.ERROR using an MQ PUT operation, so that the failure is recorded for monitoring and review

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Error Notification to Error Queue on Trigger Retrieval Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the CICS trigger retrieval fails, the captured error details must be sent to the designated error queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) to notify downstream error monitoring systems.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The CICS trigger retrieval has failed and the error notification has been sent to the error queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The termination process is invoked (8000-TERMINATION)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program closes each queue that was successfully opened — the input queue (if open), the reply/output queue (if open), and the error queue (if open) — in that sequence, and then ends the CICS transaction, preventing any further account inquiry processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initiate Program Termination After Trigger Retrieval Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a failed CICS trigger retrieval and error notification, the program must terminate gracefully by closing all queues that were opened before ending execution, ensuring no resources are left open.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has been triggered by a CICS trigger mechanism and a trigger message has been successfully retrieved containing the source queue name (MQTM-QNAME)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The CICS trigger message retrieval completes successfully (response is NORMAL)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The input queue name is set to the queue name extracted from the trigger message (MQTM-QNAME), and this queue name is used as the source for all subsequent account inquiry request messages

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract Input Queue Name from Trigger Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is triggered, the name of the input queue to read account inquiry requests from is dynamically extracted from the trigger message received via CICS. This ensures the program always reads from the correct queue as specified by the trigger.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has been triggered by a CICS trigger mechanism and a trigger message has been successfully retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The CICS trigger message retrieval completes successfully (response is NORMAL)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The reply queue name is unconditionally set to the fixed value 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT', and all account inquiry response messages will be sent to this queue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Fixed Reply Queue Name for Account Inquiry Responses
all_rules.Rule_Description: The reply queue where all account inquiry responses are sent is always fixed to CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT, regardless of the source of the request or the content of the trigger message. This ensures all account inquiry responses are routed to a single, well-known destination queue.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has successfully retrieved a CICS trigger message at startup containing a queue name (MQTM-QNAME)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program prepares to open the input queue for receiving account inquiry requests
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The input queue name is set to the queue name extracted from the trigger message (MQTM-QNAME), making it the designated source queue for all incoming account inquiry request messages

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Input Queue Name from Trigger Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: The input queue name used to receive account inquiry requests is dynamically assigned from the trigger message retrieved at program startup, ensuring the program listens on the correct queue as designated by the triggering system.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The input queue name has been set from the trigger message and the queue manager connection is established
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program requests to open the input queue for processing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The input queue is opened with shared read access (allowing multiple readers), with full message context saved (to support reply correlation), and configured to fail immediately if the queue manager is shutting down — ensuring safe and context-aware message consumption

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Input Queue in Shared Read Mode
all_rules.Rule_Description: The input queue must be opened with shared read access so that the program can receive and consume incoming account inquiry request messages. The queue is opened with context-saving capability to preserve message context for reply correlation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has requested to open the input queue in shared read mode
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The input queue is opened successfully without any errors
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The input queue handle is stored for use in subsequent message read operations, and the input queue status is marked as open and ready to receive account inquiry request messages

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Input Queue as Open and Ready to Receive Messages
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successfully opening the input queue, the program registers the queue handle and marks the input queue status as open and ready, enabling subsequent message retrieval operations to proceed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has requested to open the input queue in shared read mode
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The input queue fails to open for any reason
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The following error details are recorded: the input queue name is captured as the failing queue, the error condition code and reason code are recorded, and the error message is set to 'INP MQOPEN ERR' to identify this as an input queue open failure

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Input Queue Open Failure Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the input queue cannot be opened, the program captures the queue name and the associated error condition and reason details so that a meaningful error notification can be sent to the error queue for operational visibility.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The input queue has failed to open and error details including queue name, error condition, reason code, and error message 'INP MQOPEN ERR' have been recorded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program processes the input queue open failure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error notification containing all recorded error details is sent to the error queue 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR' so that the failure is logged and visible to operations teams

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Error Notification to Error Queue on Input Queue Open Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the input queue cannot be opened, the recorded error details must be sent to the designated error queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) to notify operations of the failure before the program terminates.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The input queue has failed to open and the error notification has been sent to the error queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program completes error notification for the input queue open failure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program initiates graceful termination by closing all queues that were successfully opened prior to the failure (including the error queue), and then exits — no account inquiry processing takes place

all_rules.Rule_Name: Terminate Program on Input Queue Open Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the input queue cannot be opened, the program cannot receive any account inquiry requests and must terminate gracefully, closing all previously opened queues before exiting.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has successfully opened the error queue and retrieved the trigger message identifying the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program prepares to open the output reply queue for account inquiry responses
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The reply queue name must be set to the fixed value 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT', which is the designated destination for all account inquiry response messages

all_rules.Rule_Name: Fixed Reply Queue Name Assignment for Account Inquiry Responses
all_rules.Rule_Description: The reply queue name for sending account inquiry responses is always fixed as CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT and is set before attempting to open the queue.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The reply queue name has been set to 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT' and the queue manager connection is active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program requests to open the reply queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The reply queue must be opened in write (output) mode with full message context passing enabled, so that response messages carry the original request context for the receiving application to correlate

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reply Queue Opened in Write Mode for Account Inquiry Responses
all_rules.Rule_Description: The reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT must be opened in write/output mode with context passing enabled so that account inquiry response messages can be placed onto it.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has requested to open the reply queue 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT' in write mode
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The reply queue opens successfully without any errors
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The reply queue must be flagged as open and ready to accept account inquiry response messages, and the queue handle must be saved for use during message put operations throughout the session

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reply Queue Successfully Opened and Marked Ready
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the reply queue is successfully opened, it is marked as available and its handle is saved so that subsequent account inquiry response messages can be placed onto it.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has requested to open the reply queue 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT' in write mode
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The reply queue fails to open for any reason
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must record all of the following error details: the queue name ('CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT'), a descriptive error message ('OUT MQOPEN ERR'), the condition code returned by the queue manager, and the reason code returned by the queue manager

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Error Details When Reply Queue Cannot Be Opened
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the reply queue fails to open, the system must capture the queue name, a descriptive error message, the condition code, and the reason code to provide a complete error record for diagnosis.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The reply queue 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT' has failed to open and error details including queue name, error description, condition code, and reason code have been captured
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The error notification process is triggered due to the reply queue open failure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The complete error details must be sent as a message to the error queue 'CARD.DEMO.ERROR', and the program must immediately terminate by closing all queues that are currently open (input queue, error queue) and ending the session — no further account inquiry processing may occur

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Error Notification and Terminate When Reply Queue Cannot Be Opened
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the reply queue cannot be opened, the captured error details must be sent to the designated error queue CARD.DEMO.ERROR and the program must terminate, as no account inquiry responses can be delivered without a functioning reply queue.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has successfully opened the Account Inquiry input queue and is ready to retrieve the next message
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A message retrieval attempt is initiated from the Account Inquiry input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must apply a maximum wait interval of 5,000 milliseconds (5 seconds) before considering the queue empty or unavailable

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Wait Interval for Queue Message Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: When attempting to retrieve a message from the Account Inquiry input queue, the system must wait up to 5 seconds before declaring no message is available, ensuring transient delays do not prematurely terminate processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is preparing to retrieve a message from the Account Inquiry input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The message retrieval parameters are configured prior to reading the queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Both the Message ID filter and the Correlation ID filter must be cleared (set to blank/none) so that any available message in the queue is eligible for retrieval, without restricting to a specific message or conversation thread

all_rules.Rule_Name: Accept Any Message Without Filter Constraints
all_rules.Rule_Description: When retrieving a message from the Account Inquiry input queue, no specific Message ID or Correlation ID filters are applied, ensuring the program accepts any available account inquiry request regardless of its origin or correlation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is preparing to retrieve an account inquiry request message from the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The message buffer is configured before the retrieval attempt
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message buffer size must be set to exactly 1,000 bytes, which defines the maximum size of an account inquiry request message that can be received and processed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Message Buffer Capacity for Account Inquiry Requests
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each account inquiry request message retrieved from the input queue must be accommodated within a fixed buffer capacity of 1,000 bytes, defining the maximum allowable size of an incoming account inquiry request.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Inquiry input queue is open, the wait interval is set to 5 seconds, message ID and correlation ID filters are cleared, and the message buffer is set to 1,000 bytes
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to retrieve the next available account inquiry request message from the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must read the next available message from the Account Inquiry input queue using the configured parameters, capturing the message content into the 1,000-byte buffer for subsequent processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Account Inquiry Request from Input Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program must actively retrieve account inquiry request messages from the designated Account Inquiry input queue using the configured wait interval, message filters, and buffer settings to obtain the next message for processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to retrieve a message from the Account Inquiry input queue with a 5-second wait interval
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A message is successfully retrieved from the input queue (retrieval condition code is OK)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The retrieved message must be marked as ready for processing and the program must proceed to the account inquiry message processing loop to handle the request

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed to Message Processing When Message Successfully Retrieved
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a message is successfully retrieved from the Account Inquiry input queue within the 5-second wait window, the program must proceed to the account inquiry processing loop to handle the request.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to retrieve a message from the Account Inquiry input queue with a 5-second wait interval
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No message is available in the input queue within the 5-second wait period (queue is empty or wait timeout is reached)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The No-More-Messages flag must be set to indicate that there are no further account inquiry requests to process, and the program must exit the message processing loop and proceed to program termination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Terminate Message Processing When No Message Available Within Wait Period
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no account inquiry request message is available in the input queue within the 5-second wait period, the program must signal that all messages have been processed and proceed to program termination, ensuring no indefinite waiting occurs.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The input queue has been successfully opened and the program has completed initial setup, and the NO-MORE-MSGS flag is not yet set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The message processing loop is active and iterating over messages from the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must repeatedly execute the message processing cycle — committing the current transaction, waiting for the next message, and processing it — until the NO-MORE-MSGS condition is raised, at which point the loop exits and the program proceeds to termination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Continuous Message Processing Until Queue is Empty
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program continuously loops to process account inquiry messages from the input queue. Each iteration commits the prior transaction and attempts to retrieve the next message. The loop exits only when no more messages are available on the queue.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The message processing loop has started a new iteration after processing a prior message (or at the very first iteration after initialization)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program begins a new cycle within the message processing loop
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A synchronization point (SYNCPOINT) must be issued to commit all work from the prior transaction cycle before any attempt is made to retrieve the next message from the input queue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Commit Before Each New Message Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the start of each iteration of the message processing loop, the program commits all work performed in the previous cycle before attempting to retrieve the next message. This ensures that each processed message's reply is permanently saved before the next message is fetched.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction syncpoint has been committed and the program is ready to retrieve the next message from the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to get the next message from the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must wait up to 5,000 milliseconds (5 seconds) for a message to become available on the input queue; the message retrieval must target the dynamically assigned input queue using its established handle, and both the message ID and correlation ID filters must be cleared so that any available message can be retrieved

all_rules.Rule_Name: Message Retrieval with 5-Second Wait Interval
all_rules.Rule_Description: When attempting to retrieve the next account inquiry message, the program waits on the input queue for up to 5 seconds. The message is read from the dynamically determined input queue using the established queue handle, with message ID and correlation ID reset to accept any available message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to retrieve a message from the input queue and a message was successfully received within the 5-second wait interval
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A message is available and retrieved from the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must invoke the account inquiry request processing logic (4000-PROCESS-REQUEST-REPLY) to validate the request parameters, perform the account lookup, and send the appropriate reply to the reply queue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Route to Account Inquiry Processing When Message is Available
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a message is successfully retrieved from the input queue within the wait interval, the program routes it to the account inquiry processing logic to validate the request, look up the account, and send a reply.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is in the message processing loop and has attempted to retrieve a message from the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No message is available on the input queue and the 5-second wait interval expires
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The NO-MORE-MSGS condition must be set to true, causing the message processing loop to exit, and the program must proceed to the termination routine which closes all open queues (input queue, reply queue, and error queue) in sequence before ending

all_rules.Rule_Name: Exit Message Processing Loop When No Messages Available
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no message is received from the input queue within the 5-second wait interval, the program recognizes that the queue is empty, sets the NO-MORE-MSGS condition, exits the processing loop, and proceeds to program termination.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has completed processing an account inquiry message — either by sending a successful account data reply or an invalid request error reply to the reply queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current message processing iteration completes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must loop back to the start of the message processing cycle, where it will first issue a SYNCPOINT to commit the completed transaction, and then attempt to retrieve the next message from the input queue with a fresh 5-second wait interval

all_rules.Rule_Name: Loop Back to Commit After Each Successful Message Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully processing an account inquiry message and sending the reply, the program loops back to the beginning of the message processing cycle to commit the completed transaction before attempting to retrieve the next message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new incoming message has been received from the Input Queue and is ready for processing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program begins processing the new message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Reply Message buffer must be cleared to spaces, and all Date and Time working fields must be reset to zeroes before any data extraction or validation begins

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Processing Buffers Before Message Parsing
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before processing any incoming account inquiry message, the reply message buffer and all date/time working fields must be cleared to ensure no residual data from a previous message contaminates the current processing cycle.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An incoming request message has been received from the Input Queue and the reply buffer has been cleared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program parses the incoming message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Function Code field (WS-FUNC) must be extracted from the message, representing the type of operation requested (e.g., 'INQA' for Account Inquiry)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract Function Code from Incoming Request Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: The function code (WS-FUNC) must be extracted from the incoming request message to identify the type of inquiry being requested. The expected value for an account inquiry is 'INQA'.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An incoming request message has been received and the Function Code (WS-FUNC) has been extracted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program continues parsing the incoming message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Key field (WS-KEY) must be extracted from the message, representing the unique Account ID number that identifies the account to be retrieved

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract Account Key from Incoming Request Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Key (WS-KEY) must be extracted from the incoming request message to identify the specific account to be queried. This key serves as the unique identifier used to look up the account record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Function Code (WS-FUNC) and Account Key (WS-KEY) have been extracted from the incoming request message
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program validates the extracted fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Processing proceeds to Account Inquiry only if BOTH conditions are true: (1) the Function Code equals 'INQA', AND (2) the Account Key is greater than zero. If either condition fails, the request is flagged as invalid and routed to the Invalid Request Response path

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Function Code and Account Key Are Present and Valid
all_rules.Rule_Description: Both the Function Code and Account Key extracted from the request message must meet minimum validity criteria before account inquiry processing can proceed. The Function Code must be 'INQA' and the Account Key must be a non-zero positive value. Both conditions must be satisfied simultaneously.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Function Code (WS-FUNC) has been extracted from the message and the Account Key (WS-KEY) has been extracted from the message
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Function Code equals 'INQA' AND the Account Key is greater than zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The request is recognized as a valid Account Inquiry request and processing proceeds to the Account Inquiry Validation and account file lookup stage

all_rules.Rule_Name: Route Valid Request to Account Inquiry Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: When both the Function Code equals 'INQA' and the Account Key is a valid non-zero value, the request is confirmed as a valid Account Inquiry and must be routed to the account lookup process.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Function Code (WS-FUNC) and Account Key (WS-KEY) have been extracted from the incoming request message
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Function Code does NOT equal 'INQA', OR the Account Key is zero or blank (either condition alone is sufficient to trigger this path)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: An error reply message must be constructed with the text 'INVALID REQUEST PARAMETERS ACCT ID: <WS-KEY value> FUNCTION: <WS-FUNC value>' and sent to the reply queue 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT'. The program does not terminate and continues to process the next message in the queue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Flag Invalid Request and Send Error Reply When Function Code or Account Key Is Missing or Invalid
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Function Code is not 'INQA' or the Account Key is zero or blank, the request cannot be processed as a valid account inquiry. An error reply message must be constructed containing both the invalid Account ID and the invalid Function Code, and sent back to the reply queue. Processing continues for subsequent messages.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account inquiry request message has been received from the input queue containing a function code and an account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the function code in the request
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the function code is exactly 'INQA', the request is considered valid for further processing; if the function code is anything other than 'INQA', the request is immediately rejected as invalid and an error response is prepared

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Account Inquiry Function Code
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must verify that the incoming request specifies the Account Inquiry function code 'INQA' before any account data retrieval is attempted. Requests carrying any other function code are rejected as invalid.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account inquiry request message has been received with function code 'INQA' already confirmed as valid
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the account ID value in the request
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the account ID is greater than zero, the request is considered fully valid and proceeds to account data retrieval; if the account ID is zero or blank, the request is rejected as invalid and an error response is prepared

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Account ID is Non-Zero
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must verify that the account ID provided in the request is a non-zero positive value. A zero or blank account ID is not a valid identifier for account data retrieval.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account inquiry request message has been received from the input queue containing a function code (WS-FUNC) and an account ID key (WS-KEY)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates both conditions together: function code equals 'INQA' AND account ID is greater than zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Only when both conditions are met simultaneously does the system proceed to retrieve account data; if either the function code is not 'INQA' or the account ID is zero or blank (or both fail), the system treats the request as invalid and routes to error response building

all_rules.Rule_Name: Both Function Code and Account ID Must Be Valid to Proceed
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system enforces that both the function code equals 'INQA' AND the account ID is greater than zero must be satisfied simultaneously. If either condition fails, the request is treated as invalid and no account data retrieval is performed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account inquiry request has failed validation because either the function code is not 'INQA' or the account ID is zero or blank
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system builds the error response message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error response message must contain the literal text 'INVALID REQUEST PARAMETERS' followed by the label 'ACCT ID :' with the actual account ID value received in the request, and the label 'FUNCTION :' with the actual function code value received in the request, all concatenated into a single reply message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Build Invalid Request Error Response with Received Parameters
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a request fails validation (invalid function code or zero account ID), the system constructs an error response message that echoes back the exact account ID and function code that were received in the invalid request, so the requesting system can identify what was wrong.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An invalid request error response message has been built containing the received account ID and function code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the error response
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error response message is placed onto the reply queue 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT' with the original message ID and correlation ID from the incoming request preserved in the reply, ensuring the requesting system can correlate the error response back to its original inquiry; after successful delivery the program continues processing the next message from the input queue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Invalid Request Error Response to Reply Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: After building the invalid request error response message, the system must deliver it to the designated reply queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT) so the requesting system receives notification of the invalid request. The reply is sent with the original message correlation identifiers preserved to allow the requester to match the response to their original request.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account inquiry request has been received with a non-zero Account ID (WS-KEY) and a valid function code of 'INQA'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to look up the account record in the ACCTDAT file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account ID from the request (WS-KEY) must be assigned as the record search key (WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID) before the file lookup is performed, ensuring the correct account record is targeted

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account ID Used as File Search Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: The account ID value received in the inquiry request must be set as the key used to search for the account record in the ACCTDAT file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account ID has been set as the file search key and the ACCTDAT file is accessible
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes a read operation against the ACCTDAT file using the Account ID as the record key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the full account record matching the provided Account ID from the ACCTDAT file, and the search result (found or not found) is captured for subsequent processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Record Search in ACCTDAT File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must perform a direct key-based lookup of the account record from the ACCTDAT account file using the Account ID as the unique record identifier.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A search for the account record in the ACCTDAT file has been completed using the provided Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the result of the account record search
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the account record is found (search result = NORMAL), the system proceeds to retrieve all account details and build the account data response; if the account record is not found (search result = NOT FOUND), the system proceeds to prepare an account not found error response

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Record Search Result Decision
all_rules.Rule_Description: After searching the ACCTDAT file, the system must evaluate the search outcome and route processing to either the account data response path (if found) or the account not found response path (if not found).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account record search in the ACCTDAT file returned a successful match for the provided Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system retrieves the account record data
