Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must extract and store all of the following account details from the retrieved record: Account ID, Account Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Account Open Date, Account Expiration Date, Account Reissue Date, Current Cycle Credit Balance, Current Cycle Debit Balance, and Account Group ID — and then proceed to build the account data response (Business Process 12)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Record Found - Retrieve All Account Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account record is successfully located in the ACCTDAT file, all relevant account data fields must be extracted from the record and made available for building the inquiry response.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account record search in the ACCTDAT file found no matching record for the provided Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines the account does not exist in the ACCTDAT file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must prepare an error response message stating 'INVALID REQUEST PARAMETERS ACCT ID: <account_id>' using the Account ID from the original request, and proceed to the Account Not Found Response process (Business Process 13)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Record Not Found - Prepare Not Found Indicator
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the provided Account ID does not match any record in the ACCTDAT file, the system must prepare an appropriate not-found error indicator message to be returned to the requester.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been successfully retrieved from the Account Data file (ACCTDAT) using the requested Account ID as the lookup key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins building the account inquiry response message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account ID value from the retrieved account record (ACCT-ID) must be populated into the Account ID field of the response message (WS-ACCT-ID)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Account ID in Response Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account record is successfully retrieved from the Account Data file (ACCTDAT), the Account ID from the retrieved record must be placed into the response message to be returned to the requester.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been successfully retrieved from the Account Data file (ACCTDAT) using the requested Account ID as the lookup key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the account active status field in the response message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Active Status value from the retrieved account record (ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS) must be populated into the Active Status field of the response message (WS-ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Account Active Status in Response Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account record is successfully retrieved from the Account Data file (ACCTDAT), the Account Active Status from the retrieved record must be placed into the response message to indicate whether the account is currently active.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been successfully retrieved from the Account Data file (ACCTDAT) using the requested Account ID as the lookup key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the current balance field in the response message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Current Balance value from the retrieved account record (ACCT-CURR-BAL) must be populated into the Current Balance field of the response message (WS-ACCT-CURR-BAL)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Current Balance in Response Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account record is successfully retrieved from the Account Data file (ACCTDAT), the Current Balance from the retrieved record must be placed into the response message to reflect the account's present financial standing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been successfully retrieved from the Account Data file (ACCTDAT) using the requested Account ID as the lookup key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the credit limit field in the response message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Credit Limit value from the retrieved account record (ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT) must be populated into the Credit Limit field of the response message (WS-ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Credit Limit in Response Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account record is successfully retrieved from the Account Data file (ACCTDAT), the Credit Limit from the retrieved record must be placed into the response message to indicate the maximum credit extended to the account holder.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been successfully retrieved from the Account Data file (ACCTDAT) using the requested Account ID as the lookup key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the cash credit limit field in the response message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Cash Credit Limit value from the retrieved account record (ACCT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT) must be populated into the Cash Credit Limit field of the response message (WS-ACCT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Cash Credit Limit in Response Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account record is successfully retrieved from the Account Data file (ACCTDAT), the Cash Credit Limit from the retrieved record must be placed into the response message to indicate the maximum cash advance credit available to the account holder.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been successfully retrieved from the Account Data file (ACCTDAT) using the requested Account ID as the lookup key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the account open date field in the response message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Open Date value from the retrieved account record (ACCT-OPEN-DATE) must be populated into the Account Open Date field of the response message (WS-ACCT-OPEN-DATE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Account Open Date in Response Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account record is successfully retrieved from the Account Data file (ACCTDAT), the Account Open Date from the retrieved record must be placed into the response message to indicate when the account was originally established.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been successfully retrieved from the Account Data file (ACCTDAT) using the requested Account ID as the lookup key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the account expiration date field in the response message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Expiration Date value from the retrieved account record (ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE) must be populated into the Account Expiration Date field of the response message (WS-ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Account Expiration Date in Response Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account record is successfully retrieved from the Account Data file (ACCTDAT), the Account Expiration Date from the retrieved record must be placed into the response message to indicate when the account or associated card is due to expire.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been successfully retrieved from the Account Data file (ACCTDAT) using the requested Account ID as the lookup key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the account reissue date field in the response message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Reissue Date value from the retrieved account record (ACCT-REISSUE-DATE) must be populated into the Account Reissue Date field of the response message (WS-ACCT-REISSUE-DATE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Account Reissue Date in Response Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account record is successfully retrieved from the Account Data file (ACCTDAT), the Account Reissue Date from the retrieved record must be placed into the response message to indicate when the account or associated card was last reissued.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been successfully retrieved from the Account Data file (ACCTDAT) using the requested Account ID as the lookup key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the current cycle credit balance field in the response message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Current Cycle Credit Balance value from the retrieved account record (ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT) must be populated into the Current Cycle Credit Balance field of the response message (WS-ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Current Cycle Credit Balance in Response Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account record is successfully retrieved from the Account Data file (ACCTDAT), the Current Cycle Credit Balance from the retrieved record must be placed into the response message to reflect the total credit transactions posted in the current billing cycle.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been successfully retrieved from the Account Data file (ACCTDAT) using the requested Account ID as the lookup key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the current cycle debit balance field in the response message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Current Cycle Debit Balance value from the retrieved account record (ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT) must be populated into the Current Cycle Debit Balance field of the response message (WS-ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Current Cycle Debit Balance in Response Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account record is successfully retrieved from the Account Data file (ACCTDAT), the Current Cycle Debit Balance from the retrieved record must be placed into the response message to reflect the total debit transactions posted in the current billing cycle.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been successfully retrieved from the Account Data file (ACCTDAT) using the requested Account ID as the lookup key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the account group ID field in the response message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Group ID value from the retrieved account record (ACCT-GROUP-ID) must be populated into the Account Group ID field of the response message (WS-ACCT-GROUP-ID)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Account Group ID in Response Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account record is successfully retrieved from the Account Data file (ACCTDAT), the Account Group ID from the retrieved record must be placed into the response message to identify the group or portfolio classification to which the account belongs.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All account data fields (Account ID, Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Open Date, Expiration Date, Reissue Date, Current Cycle Credit Balance, Current Cycle Debit Balance, and Group ID) have been individually populated into the account response working storage structure (WS-ACCT-RESPONSE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system finalizes the response message assembly
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The complete account response structure (WS-ACCT-RESPONSE) must be moved into the reply message buffer (REPLY-MESSAGE) as a single assembled unit, ready for transmission to the reply queue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assemble Complete Account Response Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all individual account data fields have been populated into their respective response fields, the complete account response structure (WS-ACCT-RESPONSE) must be assembled into the final reply message buffer (REPLY-MESSAGE) that will be transmitted back to the requester.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The complete account response message has been assembled in the reply message buffer (REPLY-MESSAGE) containing all account details for the requested Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is ready to deliver the account inquiry response
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The assembled reply message must be placed onto the output reply queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT) using the original message's correlation identifiers to allow the requesting system to match the response to its original inquiry request; if the message cannot be placed on the reply queue, the error details must be sent to the error queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) and processing must terminate

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Assembled Account Response to Reply Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the complete account response message has been assembled, it must be sent to the designated reply queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT) so the requesting system can receive the account inquiry results. The reply is sent within a syncpoint scope to ensure transactional integrity.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account inquiry request with function code 'INQA' and a non-zero Account ID has been received, and the Account File lookup has returned a 'Not Found' result for the provided Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines that no account record exists for the requested Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must compose an error response message that begins with the prefix 'INVALID REQUEST PARAMETERS' followed by the label 'ACCT ID :' and the Account ID value that was not found, forming a single concatenated message string

all_rules.Rule_Name: Compose Error Response Message for Account Not Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account inquiry is performed and the requested account does not exist in the Account File, the system must compose an error response message prefixed with 'INVALID REQUEST PARAMETERS' that includes the Account ID that was not found.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is composing an error response message because the Account File lookup returned 'Not Found' for a requested Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The error response message is being built
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account ID value (WS-KEY) that was not found must be embedded within the error response message in the format: 'INVALID REQUEST PARAMETERS ACCT ID : <account_id_value>', where the account ID is the exact value that was submitted in the inquiry request

all_rules.Rule_Name: Include Not-Found Account ID in Error Response Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: The error response message for an account not found condition must explicitly include the specific Account ID that was searched for but not found, so the requesting system can identify which account was invalid.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An error response message has been composed indicating that the requested Account ID was not found, and the reply queue 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT' is open for output
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is ready to send the error response back to the requesting application
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error response message must be placed onto the reply queue 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT' with a message buffer length of 1000, preserving the original message's correlation identifiers (message ID and correlation ID) so the requesting system can match the reply to its original inquiry request, and the message format is set to string type

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Account Not Found Error Response to Reply Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: After composing the account not found error response message, the system must deliver it to the designated reply queue so the requesting application receives the outcome of its inquiry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account inquiry request message has been retrieved from the input queue, containing a function code (WS-FUNC) and an Account ID key (WS-KEY)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The function code is NOT equal to 'INQA' OR the Account ID key is zero (or blank)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The request is classified as invalid and the program proceeds to build and send an invalid request error response; no account lookup is performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Identify Invalid Account Inquiry Request
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that an incoming account inquiry request contains both a recognized function code ('INQA') and a non-zero Account ID. If either condition fails, the request is treated as invalid and an error response is triggered.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account inquiry request has been identified as invalid because the function code is not 'INQA' or the Account ID is zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program prepares the error response message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account ID value (WS-KEY) that was received in the request is captured and included in the error response message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Account ID from Invalid Request
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a request is determined to be invalid, the Account ID value submitted in the request is captured so it can be included in the error response message for traceability.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account inquiry request has been identified as invalid because the function code is not 'INQA' or the Account ID is zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program prepares the error response message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The function code value (WS-FUNC) that was received in the request is captured and included in the error response message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Function Code from Invalid Request
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a request is determined to be invalid, the function code value submitted in the request is captured so it can be included in the error response message for traceability.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account inquiry request has been identified as invalid, and both the received Account ID (WS-KEY) and function code (WS-FUNC) have been captured
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The error response message is being built
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A reply message is constructed containing the literal text 'INVALID REQUEST PARAMETERS' followed by 'ACCT ID :' and the received Account ID value, followed by 'FUNCTION :' and the received function code value, and this message is stored as the reply message (REPLY-MESSAGE) to be sent back to the requester

all_rules.Rule_Name: Build Invalid Request Error Response Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: Constructs a descriptive error response message that clearly communicates to the requesting system that the request parameters were invalid, including both the Account ID and function code that were received, to assist in diagnosing the issue.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An error response message has been built containing 'INVALID REQUEST PARAMETERS' with the received Account ID and function code, and the reply queue 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT' is open
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program sends the error response
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error response message (REPLY-MESSAGE) is placed onto the reply queue 'CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT' using the original request's message ID (SAVE-MSGID) and correlation ID (SAVE-CORELID) to allow the requesting system to match the response to its original request; the message is committed as part of the current unit of work (SYNCPOINT)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Invalid Request Error Response to Reply Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: Delivers the constructed invalid request error response message to the designated reply queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT), ensuring the requesting system receives notification that its request contained invalid parameters. The reply is correlated back to the original request using the original message identifiers.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account inquiry response (either successful account data or an invalid request error message) has been produced and is ready to be sent back to the requesting application
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the response message for delivery to the reply queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The response message content is loaded into the message buffer with a fixed buffer length of 1000 bytes; the original request's Message ID (SAVE-MSGID) is set as the outgoing message identifier; the original request's Correlation ID (SAVE-CORELID) is set as the outgoing correlation identifier; the message format is set to string type with the queue manager's default character set encoding

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prepare Account Inquiry Response for Delivery
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before placing the response onto the reply queue, the system must load the account inquiry response content into the message buffer and attach the original request's message identifier and correlation identifier so the requesting application can match the reply to its original request.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The response message buffer has been prepared with the account inquiry response content, original message correlation details, and the reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT is open for output
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system delivers the response message to the reply queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message is placed onto the CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT queue using syncpoint control (meaning delivery is only finalised when the transaction commits), with default context propagation and with the operation set to fail immediately if the queue manager is quiescing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Deliver Response Message to Reply Queue Under Syncpoint Control
all_rules.Rule_Description: The prepared response message must be placed onto the designated reply queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT under syncpoint control, ensuring the delivery is part of the current unit of work and is only committed when the overall transaction is committed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to place the account inquiry response onto the CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT reply queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The queue manager confirms the message was accepted successfully (condition code indicates OK)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The delivery outcome (condition code and reason code) is recorded, and control is returned to the message processing loop so the next incoming account inquiry request can be processed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Confirm Successful Response Delivery
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the response message is successfully placed onto the reply queue, the system acknowledges the successful delivery and returns control to the message processing loop to handle the next incoming request.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to place the account inquiry response onto the CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT reply queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The queue manager returns a non-successful condition code (delivery failed for any reason)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The failure condition code, reason code, and the reply queue name CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT are recorded; a delivery failure message 'MQPUT ERR' is set; the error details are written to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR error queue; and the program terminates by closing all open queues (input queue, reply queue, error queue) before ending the CICS transaction — no further account inquiry messages are processed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Reply Queue Delivery Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the response message cannot be delivered to the reply queue for any reason, the system must log the delivery failure details to the dedicated error queue and terminate all processing to prevent data inconsistency.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A processing error has occurred during account inquiry processing, and the following error details have been captured: an error description (e.g., 'ERROR WHILE READING ACCTFILE', 'INP MQOPEN ERR', 'OUT MQOPEN ERR', 'MQPUT ERR', 'CICS RETREIVE'), a condition code, a reason code, and the name of the queue involved in the error
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The error notification process is triggered by calling the error handling routine (9000-ERROR)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must consolidate all captured error details (error description, condition code, reason code, and queue name) from the error display area into a single formatted error message buffer of 1000 characters, ready for delivery to the error queue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Error Message for Notification
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a processing error occurs, the system must consolidate all error details — including the error description, condition code, reason code, and the name of the queue involved — into a single formatted error message before attempting to deliver it to the error queue.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A formatted error message buffer (1000 characters) has been prepared containing the error description, condition code, reason code, and queue name, and the error queue CARD.DEMO.ERROR is open and available for writing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to write the formatted error message to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR error queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error message must be delivered to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue as a string-formatted message, ensuring the error details are available for monitoring and alerting purposes

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Error Message to Error Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: The formatted error message containing all error details must be written to the dedicated error queue CARD.DEMO.ERROR so that operations and monitoring teams are alerted to the processing failure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to write the formatted error message to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The error message is delivered to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue successfully (delivery status indicates success)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must record the successful delivery confirmation by capturing the condition code and reason code returned from the delivery operation, and return control to the calling process without initiating termination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Confirm Successful Error Message Delivery
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the error message is successfully delivered to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue, the system must record the successful delivery confirmation by capturing the resulting condition and reason codes, and then return control to the calling process to allow it to continue or terminate as appropriate.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to write the formatted error message to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue, and the delivery has failed (delivery status does not indicate success)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The error message delivery to CARD.DEMO.ERROR fails for any reason
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) capture the failed delivery condition code and reason code, (2) record the error queue name (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) as the queue involved in the failure, (3) record 'MQPUT ERR' as the error description for the delivery failure, and (4) immediately initiate an orderly program shutdown by closing all open queues (input queue, reply queue, error queue — in that order, only if open) and ending the program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initiate Program Termination on Error Delivery Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the system is unable to deliver the error notification message to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue, it must capture the failure details and initiate an orderly program shutdown, as continued processing cannot be guaranteed without error visibility.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has completed processing all messages or a termination condition has been triggered, and the input queue was previously opened successfully (REPLY-QUEUE-OPEN flag is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program prepares to close the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The input queue name (INPUT-QUEUE-NAME) and its corresponding active queue handle (INPUT-QUEUE-HANDLE) are set as the target identifiers for the closure operation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Identify Input Queue for Closure
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before closing the input queue, the program identifies the correct input queue by associating the input queue name and its active handle to ensure the correct queue is targeted for closure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The input queue name and handle have been identified and the queue is currently open
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program invokes the queue close operation (MQCLOSE) using the queue manager connection, the input queue handle, and standard close options (MQCO-NONE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The queue manager processes the closure request and returns a condition code and reason code indicating success or failure

all_rules.Rule_Name: Attempt to Close Input Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program attempts to formally close the input queue using the queue manager to release the queue resource after all message processing is complete or upon termination.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to close the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The queue manager returns a successful condition code (MQCC-OK) for the close operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The condition code and reason code from the queue manager are recorded, and the program proceeds to the next step of closing the output reply queue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Input Queue Closed Successfully
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the input queue is closed without errors, the program records the successful closure outcome and proceeds to close the output reply queue.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to close the input queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The queue manager returns a condition code other than success (not MQCC-OK) for the close operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error condition code is recorded in the application condition code field, the error reason code is recorded in the application reason code field, the input queue name (INPUT-QUEUE-NAME) is recorded in the application queue name field, and the error message 'MQCLOSE ERR' is recorded in the application return message field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Log Input Queue Closure Error Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the input queue cannot be closed successfully, the program captures and records the error details including the error condition, reason, and the name of the queue that failed to close, to support error diagnosis.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The input queue closure has failed and the error details have been logged
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The closure failure condition is confirmed (condition code is not MQCC-OK)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program immediately invokes the termination routine (8000-TERMINATION), which closes any remaining open queues (output reply queue and error queue if open) and ends the program execution

all_rules.Rule_Name: Trigger Program Termination on Input Queue Closure Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the input queue fails to close, the program cannot continue normal operations and must initiate a full program termination sequence to ensure all remaining open queues are properly closed and resources are released.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program termination sequence has been initiated either due to normal end-of-messages or an error condition
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The termination routine (8000-TERMINATION) evaluates whether the input queue is open
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the REPLY-QUEUE-OPEN flag is TRUE (indicating the input queue was successfully opened), the input queue closure routine is performed; if the flag is FALSE, the input queue closure step is skipped entirely

all_rules.Rule_Name: Conditional Execution of Input Queue Closure
all_rules.Rule_Description: The input queue closure is only attempted if the input queue was successfully opened during program initialization, preventing errors from attempting to close a queue that was never opened.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has reached the termination phase and the reply output queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT) was previously opened for sending account inquiry responses
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initiates the closure of the reply output queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The reply output queue named CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT and its associated queue handle (OUTPUT-QUEUE-HANDLE) are identified and set as the target for the closure operation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Identify Reply Output Queue for Closure
all_rules.Rule_Description: During program termination, the reply output queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT) must be specifically identified and targeted for closure to ensure proper resource release.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The reply output queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT has been identified with its queue handle (OUTPUT-QUEUE-HANDLE) for closure
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The queue closure operation is executed for the reply output queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The closure operation is attempted using the queue connection handle (MQ-HCONN), the output queue handle (OUTPUT-QUEUE-HANDLE), and standard closure options (MQCO-NONE), and the resulting condition code and reason code are captured for evaluation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Attempt Closure of Reply Output Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program must invoke the queue closure operation for the reply output queue using the queue handle obtained when the queue was originally opened.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The closure operation has been executed for the reply output queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The queue closure operation completes with a successful condition code (MQCC-OK)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The reply output queue resources are released, and the resulting condition code and reason code from the closure operation are recorded as the application condition code (MQ-APPL-CONDITION-CODE) and application reason code (MQ-APPL-REASON-CODE) respectively, and processing proceeds to program termination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Successful Reply Output Queue Closure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the reply output queue is closed successfully, the program acknowledges the successful release of queue resources and records the outcome.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The closure operation has been executed for the reply output queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The queue closure operation completes with any condition code other than successful (not MQCC-OK)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The failure details are recorded as follows: the condition code from the closure attempt is stored as the application condition code (MQ-APPL-CONDITION-CODE), the reason code from the closure attempt is stored as the application reason code (MQ-APPL-REASON-CODE), the input queue name is recorded as the application queue name (MQ-APPL-QUEUE-NAME), and the error description 'MQCLOSE ERR' is recorded as the application return message (MQ-APPL-RETURN-MESSAGE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Reply Output Queue Closure Failure Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the reply output queue closure fails, the program must capture and record all relevant failure details including the queue name, error description, condition code, and reason code for diagnostic and audit purposes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The reply output queue CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT closure has failed and the failure details (condition code, reason code, queue name, and error description 'MQCLOSE ERR') have been recorded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The closure failure is confirmed with a non-successful condition code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program immediately invokes the termination routine (8000-TERMINATION) to close any remaining open queues (input queue, error queue) and end the program, without sending an error notification to the error queue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initiate Program Termination on Reply Queue Closure Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the reply output queue cannot be closed successfully, the program must immediately proceed to the termination routine to ensure all remaining resources are properly handled.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has reached the termination phase and the error queue CARD.DEMO.ERROR has been successfully opened during the current program execution (ERR-QUEUE-OPEN flag is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initiates the closure of the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue as part of the termination sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program proceeds to attempt closing the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue; if the error queue was never opened, this closure step is skipped entirely

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initiate Error Queue Closure During Program Termination
all_rules.Rule_Description: During program termination, the error queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) must be closed only if it was previously opened, to ensure proper release of queue resources.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to close the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue during the termination phase
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The queue closure operation completes successfully without any errors
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The successful closure status and associated reason details are recorded internally, the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue resources are released, and the program continues to the final termination step (CICS RETURN)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Successful Error Queue Closure Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue is successfully closed during program termination, the closure outcome is recorded and the program continues to complete its termination sequence.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to close the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue during the termination phase, and the closure operation has failed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The queue closure returns a non-successful outcome
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The failure condition details, reason details, the queue name CARD.DEMO.ERROR, and the error message 'MQCLOSE ERR' are captured; an error notification containing these details is formatted and sent to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR error queue; and the program is forced into immediate termination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Error Queue Closure Failure - Send Error Notification
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue cannot be closed during program termination, the failure details including the queue name and a closure error message must be formatted and sent as an error notification before forcing program termination.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The closure of the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue has failed during the termination phase, and the error notification has been sent
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The error notification process completes (regardless of whether the notification itself succeeded)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program forces immediate termination by closing any remaining open queues (input queue if open, output/reply queue if open) and issuing a CICS RETURN to end the program execution; no further message processing occurs

all_rules.Rule_Name: Force Program Termination After Error Queue Closure Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the error queue CARD.DEMO.ERROR cannot be closed successfully, the program must not continue normal processing and must force an immediate termination after attempting to log the error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program termination sequence has been triggered
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the Input Queue (identified by INPUT-QUEUE-NAME and INPUT-QUEUE-HANDLE) is currently in an open state
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Input Queue is open, the system proceeds to close it and release its resources; if it is already closed, the system skips the close step and moves on to check the Reply Queue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Conditional Release of Input Queue During Shutdown
all_rules.Rule_Description: During program termination, the system must check whether the Input Queue is currently open before attempting to release it, to ensure only active queue connections are closed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program termination sequence is in progress and the Input Queue (INPUT-QUEUE-NAME) is currently open with a valid queue handle (INPUT-QUEUE-HANDLE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the close operation against the Input Queue using the established queue connection
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Input Queue is successfully closed and its resources are released; if the close operation fails, the termination sequence is re-invoked to handle the failure

all_rules.Rule_Name: Release of Input Queue Resources at Shutdown
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Input Queue is confirmed open during shutdown, the system must formally close the Input Queue to release all associated message queue resources.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program termination sequence is in progress and the Input Queue check has been completed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the Reply Queue (identified by REPLY-QUEUE-NAME and OUTPUT-QUEUE-HANDLE) is currently in an open state
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Reply Queue is open, the system proceeds to close it and release its resources; if it is already closed, the system skips the close step and moves on to check the Error Queue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Conditional Release of Reply Queue During Shutdown
all_rules.Rule_Description: During program termination, the system must check whether the Reply (Output) Queue is currently open before attempting to release it, ensuring only active connections are closed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program termination sequence is in progress and the Reply Queue (REPLY-QUEUE-NAME: CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT) is currently open with a valid queue handle (OUTPUT-QUEUE-HANDLE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the close operation against the Reply Output Queue using the established queue connection
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Reply Queue is successfully closed and its resources are released; if the close operation fails, the termination sequence is re-invoked to handle the failure

all_rules.Rule_Name: Release of Reply Queue Resources at Shutdown
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Reply Queue is confirmed open during shutdown, the system must formally close the Reply Output Queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT) to release all associated message queue resources.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program termination sequence is in progress and both the Input Queue and Reply Queue checks have been completed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the Error Queue (identified by ERROR-QUEUE-NAME: CARD.DEMO.ERROR and ERROR-QUEUE-HANDLE) is currently in an open state
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Error Queue is open, the system proceeds to close it and release its resources; if it is already closed, the system skips the close step and proceeds to return control to CICS

all_rules.Rule_Name: Conditional Release of Error Queue During Shutdown
all_rules.Rule_Description: During program termination, the system must check whether the Error Queue is currently open before attempting to release it, ensuring only active connections are closed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program termination sequence is in progress and the Error Queue (ERROR-QUEUE-NAME: CARD.DEMO.ERROR) is currently open with a valid queue handle (ERROR-QUEUE-HANDLE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the close operation against the Error Queue using the established queue connection
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Error Queue is successfully closed and its resources are released; if the close operation fails, an error notification is sent to the Error Queue and the termination sequence is re-invoked

all_rules.Rule_Name: Release of Error Queue Resources at Shutdown
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Error Queue is confirmed open during shutdown, the system must formally close the Error Queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) to release all associated message queue resources.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program termination sequence has been triggered either by normal end-of-messages or by a system error condition
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs the shutdown sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must close queues in the following mandatory order: (1) Input Queue, (2) Reply Output Queue, (3) Error Queue — and only close each queue if it is currently open, skipping any queue that was never opened or already closed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Ordered Queue Closure Sequence During Shutdown
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program termination must follow a strict sequential order when closing queues: Input Queue first, then Reply Queue, then Error Queue, ensuring an orderly and complete release of all messaging resources.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All open queues (Input, Reply, and Error) have been evaluated and closed as applicable during the termination sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system has completed all queue closure operations
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control is returned to CICS and the program terminates, making no further processing of account inquiry messages

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return Control to CICS After Queue Cleanup
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all open queues have been closed, the program must formally return control to the CICS transaction manager, signaling the end of the program's execution.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid account inquiry request has been received with Function Code 'INQA' and a non-zero Account ID (WS-KEY)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system searches the ACCTDAT Account File (LIT-ACCTFILENAME) using the Account ID (WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X) as the search key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the account record from the ACCTDAT file and evaluates the search result to determine the next course of action: Record Found, Record Not Found, or Unexpected Error

all_rules.Rule_Name: Search Account Record in Account File Using Account ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system searches the ACCTDAT Account File using the Account ID provided in the inquiry request as the search key to retrieve the corresponding account record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has searched the ACCTDAT Account File using the provided Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The search result indicates the account record was found (Normal response)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system extracts and maps the following account details into the response: Account ID (ACCT-ID), Account Active Status (ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS), Current Balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL), Credit Limit (ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT), Cash Credit Limit (ACCT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT), Account Open Date (ACCT-OPEN-DATE), Account Expiration Date (ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE), Account Reissue Date (ACCT-REISSUE-DATE), Current Cycle Credit Balance (ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT), Current Cycle Debit Balance (ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT), and Account Group ID (ACCT-GROUP-ID), then proceeds to build and send the response message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract and Return Full Account Details When Account Record is Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the account record is successfully located in the ACCTDAT file, the system extracts all relevant account details and prepares them for the response message to be sent to the reply queue.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has searched the ACCTDAT Account File using the provided Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The search result indicates the account record was not found (Not Found response)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system builds an error response message with the text 'INVALID REQUEST PARAMETERS ACCT ID: <Account ID>' where Account ID is the value of WS-KEY that was searched, and proceeds to send this error response message to the reply queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT). The program does NOT terminate and continues processing subsequent messages.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Build Invalid Request Error Response When Account Record is Not Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the searched Account ID does not exist in the ACCTDAT file, the system builds an error response message indicating invalid request parameters and includes the Account ID that was not found, then sends this response to the reply queue.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has searched the ACCTDAT Account File using the provided Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The search result indicates an unexpected error (neither Normal nor Not Found response)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system captures the following error details: Condition Code (WS-RESP-CD mapped to MQ-APPL-CONDITION-CODE), Reason Code (WS-REAS-CD mapped to MQ-APPL-REASON-CODE), Queue Name (INPUT-QUEUE-NAME mapped to MQ-APPL-QUEUE-NAME), and Error Description ('ERROR WHILE READING ACCTFILE' mapped to MQ-APPL-RETURN-MESSAGE), then sends an error notification message to the error queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR), and terminates the program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Error Details and Send Error Notification on Unexpected Account File Search Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unexpected error occurs during the account file search (neither a normal result nor a not-found result), the system captures the error details including condition code, reason code, queue name, and error description, then sends an error notification to the dedicated error queue.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An unexpected error has occurred during the ACCTDAT file search and error details have been captured (Condition Code, Reason Code, Queue Name, Error Description)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system invokes the error notification process (9000-ERROR) to send the error details to the error queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sends the error notification message (MQ-ERR-DISPLAY containing all captured error details) to the error queue CARD.DEMO.ERROR using MQPUT, and upon successful delivery proceeds to terminate the program. If the MQPUT to the error queue itself fails, the error details are written to the system display and the program terminates immediately.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Error Notification Message to Error Queue on Unexpected Account File Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unexpected account file search error occurs, the system sends the captured error details as a notification message to the dedicated error queue CARD.DEMO.ERROR to ensure the error is recorded and visible for operational monitoring.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An unexpected error has occurred during the ACCTDAT file search and the error notification has been sent to the error queue CARD.DEMO.ERROR
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system invokes the termination process (8000-TERMINATION)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system closes all queues that were successfully opened prior to termination in the following order: (1) Input Queue if it was open, (2) Output/Reply Queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT) if it was open, (3) Error Queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) if it was open, and then ends program execution. No further account inquiry messages are processed.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Terminate Program After Sending Error Notification for Unexpected Account File Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: After an unexpected account file search error has been logged to the error queue, the program must terminate gracefully by closing all open queues before ending execution, ensuring no further message processing occurs.

description:
Program COACCT01 is an online CICS program that acts as a message-driven account inquiry service. It retrieves account details from the ACCTDAT CICS file based on an account ID received via an IBM MQ input queue, then formats and sends the account information (including balance, credit limit, cash limit, dates, and status) back to a reply queue. It operates in a loop processing messages until no more are available, routing errors to a dedicated error queue.
- **Execution Environment**: Online (CICS) - **Database Access**: VSAM/CICS File (ACCTDAT) - **MQ Calls**: Yes - **Module Type**: Main module
### Key Functionalities: 1: Program Initialization - Initialize working storage fields, clear input queue name, queue manager name, and queue message fields to prepare for processing 2: Error Queue Setup - Open the dedicated error queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) for writing error messages that occur during processing 3: Transaction Trigger Retrieval - Retrieve the triggering transaction information from CICS to obtain the input queue name that initiated this program 4: Input Queue Identification - Extract the input queue name from the trigger message and set the reply queue name to CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT for sending responses 5: Input Queue Open - Open the designated input queue in shared read mode to receive incoming account inquiry request messages 6: Output Reply Queue Open - Open the reply queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.ACCT) in write mode to send account inquiry responses back to requestors 7: Initial Message Retrieval - Retrieve the first available message from the input queue with a 5-second wait interval to begin processing 8: Message Processing Loop - Continuously process incoming messages from the input queue, committing each transaction via syncpoint, until no more messages are available 9: Request Message Parsing - Parse the incoming request message to extract the function code (WS-FUNC) and account key (WS-KEY) that identify the type and target of the inquiry 10: Account Inquiry Validation - Validate that the request contains function code 'INQA' and a non-zero account ID key before attempting account data retrieval 11: Account Record Lookup - Read the account record from the ACCTDAT file using the provided account ID as the key to retrieve account details 12: Account Data Response Building - When account is found, populate the response message with account details including: Account ID, Active Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Open Date, Expiration Date, Reissue Date, Current Cycle Credit Balance, Current Cycle Debit Balance, and Group ID 13: Account Not Found Response - When the requested account ID does not exist in the file, build an error response message indicating invalid request parameters with the account ID that was not found 14: Invalid Request Response - When the function code is not 'INQA' or the account key is zero, build an error response message indicating invalid request parameters including both the account ID and function code received 15: Reply Message Delivery - Put the account inquiry response message (success or error) onto the reply queue so the requesting application can receive the account information 16: Error Notification - When a processing error occurs, format and send an error message containing error details (error description, condition code, reason code, queue name) to the error queue for monitoring and alerting 17: Input Queue Closure - Close the input queue after all messages have been processed or when termination is triggered 18: Output Reply Queue Closure - Close the reply output queue during program termination to release queue resources 19: Error Queue Closure - Close the error queue during program termination to release queue resources 20: Program Termination - Perform an orderly shutdown by closing all open queues and returning control to CICS
